import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly correlated features (|r| >= 0.6)
    corr_pairs = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids[i+1:], i+1):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                corr_pairs.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # If no correlations, no mechanism
    if not corr_pairs:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build adjacency matrix and cluster
    n_feats = len(feats.ids)
    adj = np.zeros((n_feats, n_feats))
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        i, j = feats.column(a), feats.column(b)
        adj[i,j] = adj[j,i] = 1
    
    # Simple clustering approach - just pick top correlated features
    # Look for strongest correlations to form a small module
    if len(corr_pairs) > 10:  # Limit complexity
        # Take top 10 strongest correlations
        corr_pairs = corr_pairs[:10]
    
    # Collect all unique features involved in correlations
    all_features = set()
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        all_features.add(a)
        all_features.add(b)
    
    # If too many features, limit to top ones by correlation strength
    if len(all_features) > 10:
        # Just take first few features that appear in correlations
        module_features = list(all_features)[:5]
    else:
        module_features = list(all_features)
    
    if len(module_features) < 2:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Compute weighted score using first principal component
    module_data = feats.x[:, [feats.column(f) for f in module_features]]
    _, _, vt = np.linalg.svd(module_data, full_matrices=False)
    weights = vt[0] / np.linalg.norm(vt[0])
    loadings = dict(zip(module_features, weights))
    
    # Return design with just one driver
    return Design(
        drivers=(module_features[0],),
        columns=tuple(module_features),
        products=(),
        loadings=loadings
    )
